	$(KICAD) sch export netlist -o electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net $(SCH)
	@echo "Regenerated: schematic SVG, bom.csv, netlist."
	@echo "Commit the SVG — PRs touching hw must show a picture."

hwclean:
	rm -f electricalDrawing/erc.json electricalDrawing/drc.json

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The product boundary (CLAUDE.md §2.1, D-038): a grader must confirm in sixty seconds that
# the only network code is the box's own page server. This is that confirmation.
#
#   check.sh ROOT                 check ROOT/src, ROOT/include and ROOT/Makefile
#   check.sh --selftest CASES     every CASES/bad_* must fail and every CASES/good_* pass
#
# The rules, applied to *.c and *.h, comments included:
#   1. No network family, resolver or address call outside src/interface/.
#   2. No HTTP or TLS library, no Bluetooth socket header, and no shelling out, anywhere.
#   3. socket() only in src/ipc/uds.c (Unix sockets, D-042, D-043) and src/interface/.
#   4. The Makefile links no network library.
set -uo pipefail

check() {
    local root=$1 bad=0 hits
    local dirs=()
    for d in src include; do [[ -d "$root/$d" ]] && dirs+=("$root/$d"); done

    scan() {  # scan PATTERN -> "file:line:text" for every C file under src/ and include/
        [[ ${#dirs[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0
        grep -rnE --include='*.c' --include='*.h' "$1" "${dirs[@]}" 2>/dev/null
    }
    report() {  # report RULE HITS
        [[ -z "$2" ]] && return 0
        printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed "s|^$root/||; s|^|  $1: |"
        bad=1
    }

    hits=$(scan '\b(AF|PF)_(INET6?|PACKET|NETLINK)\b|\b(getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|gethostbyaddr|getnameinfo|inet_(pton|ntop|addr|aton|ntoa))\b|#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(netdb\.h|netinet/|arpa/inet\.h)' \
           | grep -v "^$root/src/interface/")
    report "network outside src/interface/" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(curl/|openssl/|bluetooth/)|\b(curl_[a-z]|SSL_[A-Za-z])|\bAF_BLUETOOTH\b|\b(popen|system)[[:space:]]*\(')
    report "HTTP, TLS, Bluetooth socket or shell" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '\bsocket(pair)?[[:space:]]*\(' \
           | grep -v -e "^$root/src/interface/" -e "^$root/src/ipc/uds\.c:")
    report "socket() outside src/ipc/uds.c and src/interface/" "$hits"

    if [[ -f "$root/Makefile" ]]; then
        hits=$(grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(LDLIBS|LDFLAGS).*-l(curl|ssl|crypto|bluetooth)\b' "$root/Makefile" \
               | sed 's|^|Makefile:|')
        report "network library linked" "$hits"
    fi
    return $bad
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--selftest" ]]; then
    cases=${2:?usage: check.sh --selftest CASES}
    fail=0
    for c in "$cases"/bad_* "$cases"/good_*; do
        name=$(basename "$c")
        if check "$c" >/dev/null; then got=pass; else got=fail; fi
        case "$name:$got" in
            bad_*:fail|good_*:pass) ;;
            *) echo "boundary self-test: $name should not $got"; fail=1 ;;
        esac
    done
    exit $fail
include/common:
log.h

include/ipc:
ring.h

include/store:
record.h
wal.h
                             v
  storaged [D]  BEGIN..COMMIT batches, 1 fsync/s, ~1 KB/s -> ext4 on SD (D-025)
    ^           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few a drive (D-042)
    | committed records only, read back from the log, ~1 s behind (D-031)
    v
  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> model -> FSM
    | verdicts over a Unix socket, a few per drive at most
    v
  supervisor [E] spawns, heartbeats, restarts with backoff --GPIO--> light,
    ^            1-4 Hz pulse = alive; steady, except yellow at boot = not running (D-027)
    | UDS, on demand
  obdctl (CLI); statusd: page + report --> phone on the box's Wi-Fi (D-013, D-043)
power: owner's USB-C charger -> power block + supercapacitor -> Pi 4 (D-024)
```

Rates are estimates until the first drive (`firstcap`); the logging tool reaches 22
requests a second on `obdsim`. One reply or probe reading is one sample, one record and
one analysis step. Queries go to the supervisor, which asks the process holding the
answer (D-043); `analyzed` never reads a ring (D-031).

> 📏 **DRIVE:** measured request rate, reply-time p50/p99 and PID count replace the
> estimates here and in §5.

## 2. Mechanism mapping

D and E are the committed pair (D-017). B and F stay declined: these rates never stress
a ring, and 1-Wire timing belongs to the kernel, not to us (D-029, D-037).

| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power can vanish at any instant (empty bank at a cold crank, pulled cable; D-024), yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn a sample a cut later erased (D-031): append-only CRC'd records, 1 s commits, A/B checkpoints (D-025, D-035) | 50 cuts of the Pi's 5 V rail mid-write; records lost per cut |

- **The control socket.** The supervisor listens on `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`, a Unix
  domain `SOCK_STREAM` socket, mode 0660. A request is one line, `VERB key=value ...`,
  at most 512 bytes. A reply is zero or more lines of `key=value` fields, then `ok`, or
  `err <code> <reason>`, then the connection closes. Text, so it can be typed by hand
  and quoted in the report and at the defense.
- **Routing.** The supervisor answers `status` itself, from its children's heartbeats.
  It forwards `verdicts`, `series` and `faults` to `storaged`, which reads its own
  committed log up to the durable offset (D-031), and `baseline` to `analyzed`, the only
  holder of baselines, each over that process's own query socket in the same format. A
  child that is down gives `err unavailable <name>`; nothing else waits on it.

**The five verbs.**

| Verb | Arguments | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | none | each process: up, down or restarting, pid, uptime, restarts, RSS, CPU, event and drop counts; each ring's depth and overruns; dongle link and probe present or absent; the light's state; whether wall time is trusted; the mix of `src` in this session |
| `verdicts` | `--since WHEN` (default: this boot) | each surfaced verdict: start, end or active, fault area, the sensors that cooperated, residual, `src` |
| `series` | `PID --from WHEN --to WHEN [--binned]` | the samples of one PID (`0C`, or `probe`) in the window, each with `src`; `--binned` gives per-bin means instead |
| `baseline` | `PID [--bin RPM,LOAD,COOLANT]` | the learned mean and variance of one PID in every bin, or in the one bin named |
| `faults` | `--since WHEN` (default: this boot) | detection, degradation and recovery events (D-042), each with `src` |

`WHEN` is ISO 8601 or relative (`-2h`). `obdctl` exits 0 on `ok`, 1 on `err`, 2 on a
usage error and 3 when the supervisor cannot be reached.

**`statusd`.** The phone page and the report generator (D-013, D-028) are one supervised
process, `statusd`, in `src/interface/`. It serves HTTP only on the box's access-point
address, and builds every page and report from the same control-socket verbs, so it holds
no state of its own. It is the only process with an `AF_INET` socket.

**Why.** Board item `ipcspec`: B.2, D-013 and D-031 all route queries through the
supervisor without saying how, the README's `baseline` line was ambiguous about bins,
and the status page had no process name for the failure table, the Makefile or the
soak's RSS plot. A line protocol over one socket is the smallest thing that lets the CLI,
the page and a human at a terminal ask the same questions. History is answered by
`storaged` because it owns the log; the supervisor does not hold data, so a query can
never slow the restart path.

**Cost.** Three query sockets (supervisor, `storaged`, `analyzed`) and their parsers,
each a place for a malformed request to be handled; every parser gets a test with bad
input. History queries cost `storaged` reads while it writes, which the CPU measurement
(D-036) will show.

**Alternative rejected.** `obdctl` reading the log files itself: simpler, but it breaks
D-031's rule that only the process holding the answer reads it, and the page would need a
second copy of that reader.

### B.12 — The rings live in shared memory the supervisor creates; `storaged` frees a slot only after `fsync` ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

/* supervisor — mechanism E.
 *
 * A diagnostic recorder that dies silently has actively harmed its user, who believes
 * it is on duty. Any child may be kill -9'd at any time; the system degrades, logs,
 * and recovers.
 *
 * The subtle requirement: a PHYSICALLY UNPLUGGED sensor is not a crash. Restarting a
 * child in a tight loop because its hardware is gone is a restart storm, and it is the
 * failure mode most likely to appear at hour 31 of the soak.
 */
#include "common/log.h"

#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    log_init("supervisor", LOG_INFO);
    LOG_I("start");

    /* TODO(M3): fork/exec children; fd hygiene across fork; waitpid loop.
     * TODO(M3): restart policy with exponential backoff + a restart-storm guard.
     * TODO(M3): hourly heartbeat per child (log_heartbeat) — the soak plot needs it.
     * TODO(M4): degrade-not-die when a sensor is absent; distinguish absent from
     *           crashed and log the distinction. Demo day will unplug something. */

    LOG_W("not implemented — M0 scaffold");
    return 0;
}
/* obdctl — query CLI over a Unix domain socket.
 *
 * The handout is explicit that a crisp CLI with exact semantics beats a pretty
 * dashboard, and it is far more extensible at the live-modification station on demo
 * day. Resist the web app.
 *
 * This is the ONLY directory in src/ permitted to contain network code, and only for
 * the LAN interface (CLAUDE.md §2.1). `make boundary` enforces that.
 */
#include "common/log.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static int usage(void)
{
    fputs("usage: obdctl <verb>\n"
          "  status                     liveness, per-process RSS, event counts\n"
          "  verdicts [--since WHEN]    current and historical diagnoses\n"
          "  series PID --from --to     raw or binned history\n"
          "  baseline PID               learned model for an operating-point bin\n"
          "  faults                     detection / degradation / recovery events\n",
          stderr);
    return 2;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    if (argc < 2) return usage();

    log_init("obdctl", LOG_WARN);

    static const char *verbs[] = { "status", "verdicts", "series", "baseline", "faults" };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof verbs / sizeof verbs[0]; i++) {
        if (strcmp(argv[1], verbs[i]) == 0) {
            /* TODO(M3): connect to the supervisor's UDS and issue the request. */
            printf("%s: not implemented — M0 scaffold\n", verbs[i]);
            return 0;
        }
    }
    return usage();
}
# carwatch — CS370 term project
# Systems core is C17 and must stay -Wall -Wextra -Werror clean (CLAUDE.md §2.4).

# CC is make's default, cc: gcc on the Pi and in CI, clang on macOS.

# The tool tests (tests/tools/, D-032) need Python 3.11 or newer, the version Raspberry Pi
# OS ships; the department machines put 3.9 on PATH as python3. Pick the first interpreter
# that is new enough; fall back to python3 so the error, if any, names the version.
PY       ?= $(shell for p in python3 python3.13 python3.12 python3.11; do \
              command -v $$p >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              $$p -c 'import sys; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 11))' >/dev/null 2>&1 && \
              { echo $$p; exit 0; }; \
            done; echo python3)
CSTD      = -std=c17
WARN      = -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wvla
OPT      ?= -O2 -g
CPPFLAGS += -Iinclude -D_GNU_SOURCE
CFLAGS   += $(CSTD) $(WARN) $(OPT)
LDLIBS   += -lm -lpthread

BUILD    = build
BIN      = $(BUILD)/bin

ALL_SRC    = $(wildcard src/*/*.c)
# Library objects: everything except the per-daemon entry points.
COMMON_SRC = $(filter-out %/main.c,$(ALL_SRC))
COMMON_OBJ = $(COMMON_SRC:%.c=$(BUILD)/%.o)

DAEMONS    = obdd storaged analyzed supervisor obdctl
DAEMON_BIN = $(addprefix $(BIN)/,$(DAEMONS))

TEST_SRC   = $(wildcard tests/test_*.c)
TEST_BIN   = $(TEST_SRC:tests/%.c=$(BIN)/%)

.PHONY: all test asan memcheck soakcheck replay deploy clean boundary boardcheck \
        hwcheck hwdocs hwclean toolcheck

all: $(DAEMON_BIN)

$(BIN)/obdd:       $(BUILD)/src/obd/main.o        $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/storaged:   $(BUILD)/src/store/main.o      $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/analyzed:   $(BUILD)/src/analysis/main.o   $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/supervisor: $(BUILD)/src/supervisor/main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)
$(BIN)/obdctl:     $(BUILD)/src/interface/main.o  $(COMMON_OBJ)

$(DAEMON_BIN):
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BUILD)/%.o: %.c
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -MMD -MP -c $< -o $@

$(BIN)/test_%: tests/test_%.c $(COMMON_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(BIN)
	$(CC) $(CPPFLAGS) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# `all` first: every daemon must compile under the same flags as the tests, so `make asan`
# builds the daemons with the sanitizers too, not only the unit tests.
test: all $(TEST_BIN) boundary boardcheck toolcheck
	@fail=0; for t in $(TEST_BIN); do \
		printf '%-28s ' "$$(basename $$t)"; \
		if $$t; then echo PASS; else echo FAIL; fail=1; fi; done; \
	exit $$fail

# CLAUDE.md §2.1 — a grader must be able to confirm the boundary in sixty seconds (D-038).
# Network code only in src/interface/; Unix sockets only through src/ipc/uds.c. The
# check tests itself first: every case under tests/boundary/cases/bad_* must fail.
boundary:
	@tests/boundary/check.sh --selftest tests/boundary/cases
	@tests/boundary/check.sh . && echo "boundary                     PASS"

# docs/milestones.md is the board (D-020) - every task, question and decision
# in the project is a checkbox there. Validate it in the same gate as the C.
boardcheck:
	@$(PY) tools/test_board.py

# Python tool tests (stdlib unittest, tests/tools/). The venv is made on first use, and
# refreshed when a requirements file changes, so a fresh clone stays green; it needs the
# network for that install. Dev only (D-032).
.venv/.installed: tools/requirements.txt tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@test -x .venv/bin/python || $(PY) -m venv .venv
	@.venv/bin/pip install -q -r tools/requirements-analysis.txt
	@touch $@

toolcheck: .venv/.installed
	@PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests/tools -q && \
		echo "toolcheck                    PASS"

# Sanitized objects live in their own tree. Objects do not depend on the flags that built
# them, so sharing build/ let a plain `make` link against ASan objects and fail, and let
# `make test` rerun sanitized binaries without saying so.
# -fno-sanitize-recover makes a UBSan finding abort the test, so it cannot print PASS.
# LeakSanitizer is on by default on Linux (the Pi, CI); macOS arm64 does not have it.
asan:
	$(MAKE) BUILD=$(BUILD)/asan test \
	  OPT="-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer"

memcheck: $(TEST_BIN)
	@command -v valgrind >/dev/null 2>&1 || { \
		echo "valgrind not found: run make memcheck on the Pi or Linux (macOS has none)"; exit 1; }
	@for t in $(TEST_BIN); do valgrind --error-exitcode=1 --leak-check=full $$t || exit 1; done

soakcheck: all
	./soak/run_soak.sh --mini

replay: all
	@test -n "$(FIX)" || { echo "usage: make replay FIX=fixtures/<name>"; exit 1; }
	./tools/replay.py --fixture $(FIX) --label replay

deploy: all
	@test -n "$(PI)" || { echo "usage: make deploy PI=pi@<host>"; exit 1; }
	@# Source only: no build trees, no Mac venv, no raw drive data or soak logs, no transcripts.
	rsync -a --exclude /build --exclude /.git --exclude /.venv --exclude /data \
	      --exclude /soak/logs --exclude /partners ./ $(PI):~/carwatch/
	ssh $(PI) 'cd ~/carwatch && make'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- hardware
# KiCad 10. On Windows kicad-cli.exe is under
# "C:/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/" and is NOT on PATH by default:
#   make hwcheck KICAD="/c/Program Files/KiCad/10.0/bin/kicad-cli.exe"
KICAD ?= kicad-cli
SCH    = electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.kicad_sch

# ERC as a build failure — the hardware equivalent of -Werror (CLAUDE.md 7.12).
hwcheck:

	$(KICAD) sch erc --exit-code-violations --format json \

# Regenerate everything derived from the schematic. Never hand-edit the outputs.
hwdocs:
	@mkdir -p docs/figures
	$(KICAD) sch export svg --exclude-drawing-sheet -o docs/figures/ $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export bom \
	         --fields "Reference,Value,Footprint,MPN,Datasheet,Qty" \
	         --group-by Value -o docs/hardware/bom.csv $(SCH)
	$(KICAD) sch export netlist -o electricalDrawing/electricalDrawing.net $(SCH)
	@echo "Regenerated: schematic SVG, bom.csv, netlist."
	@echo "Commit the SVG — PRs touching hw must show a picture."

hwclean:
	rm -f electricalDrawing/erc.json electricalDrawing/drc.json

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The product boundary (CLAUDE.md §2.1, D-038): a grader must confirm in sixty seconds that
# the only network code is the box's own page server. This is that confirmation.
#
#   check.sh ROOT                 check ROOT/src, ROOT/include and ROOT/Makefile
#   check.sh --selftest CASES     every CASES/bad_* must fail and every CASES/good_* pass
#
# The rules, applied to *.c and *.h, comments included:
#   1. No network family, resolver or address call outside src/interface/.
#   2. No HTTP or TLS library, no Bluetooth socket header, and no shelling out, anywhere.
#   3. socket() only in src/ipc/uds.c (Unix sockets, D-042, D-043) and src/interface/.
#   4. The Makefile links no network library.
set -uo pipefail

check() {
    local root=$1 bad=0 hits
    local dirs=()
    for d in src include; do [[ -d "$root/$d" ]] && dirs+=("$root/$d"); done

    scan() {  # scan PATTERN -> "file:line:text" for every C file under src/ and include/
        [[ ${#dirs[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0
        grep -rnE --include='*.c' --include='*.h' "$1" "${dirs[@]}" 2>/dev/null
    }
    report() {  # report RULE HITS
        [[ -z "$2" ]] && return 0
        printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed "s|^$root/||; s|^|  $1: |"
        bad=1
    }

    hits=$(scan '\b(AF|PF)_(INET6?|PACKET|NETLINK)\b|\b(getaddrinfo|gethostbyname|gethostbyaddr|getnameinfo|inet_(pton|ntop|addr|aton|ntoa))\b|#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(netdb\.h|netinet/|arpa/inet\.h)' \
           | grep -v "^$root/src/interface/")
    report "network outside src/interface/" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '#[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]*<(curl/|openssl/|bluetooth/)|\b(curl_[a-z]|SSL_[A-Za-z])|\bAF_BLUETOOTH\b|\b(popen|system)[[:space:]]*\(')
    report "HTTP, TLS, Bluetooth socket or shell" "$hits"

    hits=$(scan '\bsocket(pair)?[[:space:]]*\(' \
           | grep -v -e "^$root/src/interface/" -e "^$root/src/ipc/uds\.c:")
    report "socket() outside src/ipc/uds.c and src/interface/" "$hits"

    if [[ -f "$root/Makefile" ]]; then
        hits=$(grep -nE '^[[:space:]]*(LDLIBS|LDFLAGS).*-l(curl|ssl|crypto|bluetooth)\b' "$root/Makefile" \
               | sed 's|^|Makefile:|')
        report "network library linked" "$hits"
    fi
    return $bad
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--selftest" ]]; then
    cases=${2:?usage: check.sh --selftest CASES}
    fail=0
    for c in "$cases"/bad_* "$cases"/good_*; do
        name=$(basename "$c")
        if check "$c" >/dev/null; then got=pass; else got=fail; fi
        case "$name:$got" in
            bad_*:fail|good_*:pass) ;;
            *) echo "boundary self-test: $name should not $got"; fail=1 ;;
        esac
    done
    exit $fail
include/common:
log.h

include/ipc:
ring.h

include/store:
record.h
wal.h
                             v
  storaged [D]  BEGIN..COMMIT batches, 1 fsync/s, ~1 KB/s -> ext4 on SD (D-025)
    ^           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few a drive (D-042)
    | committed records only, read back from the log, ~1 s behind (D-031)
    v
  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> model -> FSM
    | verdicts over a Unix socket, a few per drive at most
    v
  supervisor [E] spawns, heartbeats, restarts with backoff --GPIO--> light,
    ^            1-4 Hz pulse = alive; steady, except yellow at boot = not running (D-027)
    | UDS, on demand
  obdctl (CLI); statusd: page + report --> phone on the box's Wi-Fi (D-013, D-043)
power: owner's USB-C charger -> power block + supercapacitor -> Pi 4 (D-024)
```

Rates are estimates until the first drive (`firstcap`); the logging tool reaches 22
requests a second on `obdsim`. One reply or probe reading is one sample, one record and
one analysis step. Queries go to the supervisor, which asks the process holding the
answer (D-043); `analyzed` never reads a ring (D-031).

> 📏 **DRIVE:** measured request rate, reply-time p50/p99 and PID count replace the
> estimates here and in §5.

## 2. Mechanism mapping

D and E are the committed pair (D-017). B and F stay declined: these rates never stress
a ring, and 1-Wire timing belongs to the kernel, not to us (D-029, D-037).

| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power can vanish at any instant (empty bank at a cold crank, pulled cable; D-024), yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn a sample a cut later erased (D-031): append-only CRC'd records, 1 s commits, A/B checkpoints (D-025, D-035) | 50 cuts of the Pi's 5 V rail mid-write; records lost per cut |

/* Structured logging. Every line is machine-parseable, because the 48-hour soak log
 * is a graded deliverable and we will have to plot it. (handout §3.4) */
#ifndef CARWATCH_LOG_H
#define CARWATCH_LOG_H

#include <stdint.h>

typedef enum { LOG_DEBUG, LOG_INFO, LOG_WARN, LOG_ERROR, LOG_FATAL } log_level_t;

/* Data provenance. CLAUDE.md §2.7: replayed or synthesized data is labeled as such
 * EVERYWHERE it appears. This field exists from day one so that it is impossible to
 * forget later. Zero is not a label (D-040): memory nobody labeled reads as invalid,
 * never as live. */
typedef enum { SRC_INVALID = 0, SRC_LIVE = 1, SRC_REPLAY = 2, SRC_SYNTH = 3 } data_src_t;

#define SRC_IS_VALID(s) ((s) >= SRC_LIVE && (s) <= SRC_SYNTH)

void        log_init(const char *component, log_level_t min);
void        log_set_src(data_src_t src);
data_src_t  log_get_src(void);
const char *log_src_name(data_src_t src);

void log_emit(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)

# Plan: `statusd`, the on-box status website (dummy data first)

## Context

D-013/D-028/D-043 already name this process: `statusd`, C, in `src/interface/`, the only
`AF_INET` process, serving the phone page over the box's own Wi-Fi. Board item `statusd`
(#177, "runs as a supervised child and is built by the Makefile") is the open box;
`phoneview` (M4) and `report` (M3) are the later content items. Today there is no server
code at all. The goal now: a working site showing faults/verdicts, process health, trends
and a CSV report, fed by **synthetic** values behind a seam, so the real OBD2/analysis data
plugs in later with no page changes.

Decisions already made with the user: server in **C** (matches D-043); **standalone
binary now**, supervisor spawning stays with `supfork` (#41); page scope = faults list,
process health, trends + CSV. A small "latest values" strip is included because trends are
meaningless without current readings (flag in review if unwanted).

## Design

**The seam (the whole point).** D-043 says the page is built from control-socket verbs
(`status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`; reply = `key=value` lines then `ok`). So
`statusd` talks to a *source* with one function: `source_query(verb, args, out_buf)`
returning exactly that D-043 text. Two implementations behind one header:
- `synth_source.c` (now): deterministic fake data, every record `src=synth`.
- `ctl_source.c` (later, not in this PR): connects to `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`.
Swapping = one line in `statusd_main.c`. No page or HTTP code changes.

**Routes** (HTTP/1.1, GET only, `Connection: close`, single-threaded `poll()`):

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | static page (HTML+CSS+JS embedded as C strings, no CDN: device is offline) |
| `/api/status` `/api/verdicts` `/api/series?pid=0C&from=..&to=..` `/api/faults` | the verb reply converted to JSON |
| `/report.csv` | CSV built from `series`+`verdicts`, `src` column on every row |
| anything else | 404; non-GET 405; oversized/malformed request 400 |

**Page.** Four panels, polled every 2 s with `fetch`: Latest values, Verdicts/faults
(active vs. past, fault area, cooperating sensors, residual), Process health
(supervisor/obdd/storaged/analyzed/statusd: up/down, uptime, restarts, RSS, ring depth),
Trends (inline-SVG sparklines per PID, drawn by ~60 lines of vanilla JS; no libraries).
A persistent banner shows **SYNTHETIC DATA** whenever any row has `src=synth` (CLAUDE.md
§2.7). Link to `/report.csv`. Read-only, no forms.

**Binding.** Default `127.0.0.1:8080` for development; `--bind ADDR` / `--port N` for the
AP address on the Pi (never defaults to `0.0.0.0`). Logs via `common/log.h`
(`log_init("statusd", ...)`, `log_set_src(SRC_SYNTH)`), every syscall error logged,
`goto`-cleanup, every allocation checked, no VLAs. SIGTERM exits 0 cleanly, heartbeat
via `log_heartbeat` so it is supervisable later (§2.6).

## Files

New (all under `src/interface/` unless noted):
- `statusd_main.c`: arg parsing, listen socket, poll loop, signals.
- `http.c` + `include/interface/http.h`: request-line parser and response writer (bounded buffers, header size cap, timeouts on slow clients).
- `source.h`: the seam; `synth_source.c`: fake data (sine/random-walk RPM, speed, coolant, load, probe temp; 2 fake verdicts e.g. "cooling" and "intake/vacuum"; 5 fake process rows).
- `kv.c` + `include/interface/kv.h`: parse D-043 `key=value` reply lines; `json.c`: tiny JSON writer with escaping.
- `page.c`: embedded HTML/CSS/JS (or `src/interface/page/*.html` + a `make`-time generator, only if the embedded string gets unwieldy).
- Tests (same commit as each unit): `tests/test_http.c` (good/bad/oversized/partial requests), `tests/test_kv.c`, `tests/test_json.c` (escaping), `tests/test_statusd.c` (start on an ephemeral port, GET each route, check 200/404/405, `src=synth` present, CSV header).

Edits:
- `Makefile`: add `statusd` to `DAEMONS`, link rule `$(BIN)/statusd: $(BUILD)/src/interface/statusd_main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)`; change `COMMON_SRC` filter from `%/main.c` to `%main.c` so `statusd_main.c` stays out of the library; add `make run-status`.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: new ⚠️ UNREVIEWED entry (next free ID, "synthetic source seam; `statusd` standalone until `supfork`") **in the same commit as the code**, plus Review Queue row; `docs/DESIGN.md` §1 note; `docs/milestones.md`: add open boxes only (e.g. `ctlsource`: replace synth source with ctl.sock client; `statusspawn`: supervisor spawns statusd), never tick `statusd`. Then `python tools/board_sync.py`.
- `tests/boundary/`: no rule change expected (AF_INET only in `src/interface/` already passes); run it to confirm, and add a `good_` case only if the checker needs one.

Reuse: `common/log.h` (logging, `data_src_t`/`SRC_SYNTH`, `log_heartbeat`); `Makefile` test globbing picks up new `tests/test_*.c` automatically; existing `tools/obdsim.py` is *not* used (that emulates the adapter, a different layer).

## Commit sequence (CLAUDE.md §7; branch `lance/m3/statusd`, draft PR at first commit)

Session is **Lance's**. Branch from fresh `main` before any edit. Stage explicit paths only.
1. `M3 interface: parse HTTP requests and write responses` (http.c + test)
2. `M3 interface: parse D-043 reply lines and write JSON` (kv.c, json.c + tests)
3. `M3 interface: synthetic source behind the control-socket seam` (source.h, synth_source.c + test, labeled synth)
4. `M3 interface: serve the status API and CSV report from statusd` (statusd_main.c, routes, Makefile, integration test, D-0xx draft decision)
5. `M3 interface: status page with faults, process health and trends` (page.c)
6. `M3 docs: board boxes for the real source and supervisor spawn`

Each commit builds and passes tests alone; commit 4 may exceed 400 lines and will say why in `WHY`.

## Verification

- `make`, `make test` (includes `boundary`, `boardcheck`, `toolcheck`), `make asan`: all green, output pasted in the PR. Note `python` is not on PATH here (only `python3`), so run `python3 tools/board_sync.py`.
- Manual: `make run-status`, open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`; confirm the SYNTHETIC banner, panels update every 2 s, `curl -i` each route, `curl /report.csv | head` shows `src=synth` on every row, bad inputs (`printf 'GARBAGE\r\n\r\n' | nc 127.0.0.1 8080`, a 100 KB header, a slow client) get 400/closed without crashing.
- `kill -TERM` exits 0; `kill -9` leaves no stray fds (`ls /proc/<pid>/fd` before/after).
- Run with the network unplugged on loopback to confirm no outbound calls (`ss -tp` shows only the listener).

## Least sure about / for review

- Single-threaded `poll()` is enough for one phone; a slow client is handled by a per-connection deadline, which needs a test.
- Embedded page strings are reviewable but awkward; split to files if it passes ~300 lines.
- The "latest values" strip was not in the chosen scope; cheap to drop.
- The new decision is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED until Camden or Lance signs it.

**Recommendation: no server library, and no front-end libraries.** I'd write a small GET-only server on `poll()`, about 300 lines, with a vanilla HTML, CSS and JS page.

## C HTTP server

| Option | License / size | Fit here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hand-written (`poll()` + our parser)** | ours, ~300 lines | Fits every constraint. One client (a phone) and read-only GET is a tiny problem. We can explain every line at the defense and change it live at the modification station (rubric §6). |
| libmicrohttpd | LGPL, system package | Solid and small. It adds a link-time dependency and threading we don't need. It also pulls us toward the `LDLIBS` lines that `make boundary` scans. |
| Mongoose | GPLv2 or commercial, single file | Easy to drop in. The file contains an HTTP *client*, TLS and MQTT. That breaks "`src/` contains no HTTP client, ever" and the sixty-second grader grep. The license is also awkward. |
| CivetWeb | MIT, large | Same problem: it bundles client code and a lot of surface. |
| libevent `evhttp`, h2o, facil.io, libonion | various | Too heavy. They bring event-loop frameworks for a one-phone page. |
| picohttpparser | MIT, ~300 lines | Only a request parser, so it is reasonable. But a GET-only parser is about 80 lines, and handout §3 and CLAUDE.md §2.2 favor code we wrote. |

My reasons for hand-writing it:
- **Boundary and grading.** The graded claims are "no network code outside `src/interface/`" and "inference is C we wrote". A vendored web framework dilutes both, and every dependency is something the reviewer has to understand (§7.6).
- **Defense value.** HTTP request parsing, partial reads and slow-client deadlines are real systems-programming content we can show off.
- **Risk.** The main risk is parser bugs. We cover that with bad-input tests and ASan/UBSan, which the plan already includes.

If we later want HTTP/1.1 keep-alive or TLS, I'd revisit it. The box is a closed WPA2 network with no upstream, so I don't think we will.

## Front end

The device has no internet, so any library has to be vendored into the repo anyway.

| Need | Library option | Cost | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Charts | Chart.js (~200 KB min), uPlot (~50 KB), D3 (~280 KB) | Large for 4–6 sparklines | **Inline SVG**, ~60 lines of JS. Sparklines and a few gauges need only `<polyline>`. |
| DOM updates | React/Preact (~4–40 KB), htmx (~14 KB), Alpine (~15 KB) | Build tooling or a vendored blob | **`fetch()` + `textContent`/`innerHTML`.** Four panels polled every 2 s don't need a framework. |
| CSS | Bootstrap (~160 KB), Tailwind (needs a build step), Pico.css (~10 KB) | Large, or a build step | **~100 lines of hand-written CSS** with custom properties. A flex/grid layout plus `prefers-color-scheme` covers a phone in a car at night. |

How I'd build the front end:
- Embed the page in the binary as C string literals (or `xxd -i`) so there's one artifact and no file serving. This also removes path-traversal risk, because there is no file-serving code.
- Use `viewport` meta and a single-column layout at phone width. Make fault severity readable without color alone, since it's a dashboard in a car.
- Keep the **SYNTHETIC DATA** banner (§2.7) driven by the `src` field, so it disappears by itself when real data arrives.

The one thing I'd reconsider is charts, if we later want zoom, tooltips or a pan across hours of history. At that point uPlot is the smallest credible option. For the first cut, SVG is enough.

lets look more at iuPlot and what it would include if we were to use it.

This is from memory, so verify the exact figures against the release before we commit to anything. I can fetch the repo and check if you want.

## What uPlot is
- A canvas-2D time-series charting library by Leon Sorokin, MIT licensed, with zero dependencies.
- Two files: `uPlot.iife.min.js` (~48 KB, roughly 20 KB gzipped) and `uPlot.min.css` (~2 KB).
- It's built to be fast with large datasets. It can draw 100k+ points per series smoothly, and its docs claim the best speed and size among the common chart libraries.

## What you get
- **Chart types:** lines, area fills, bars and stepped lines, all on a time axis.
- **Axes and scales:** multiple Y scales (RPM next to coolant °C next to speed), auto-ranging, custom tick and label formatting, and local or UTC time axes.
- **Cursor and legend:** crosshair, live legend values on hover, and drag-to-zoom (double-click resets).
- **Layout:** `setSize()` for responsive resize, and `uPlot.sync()` to link cursors and zoom across several charts, e.g. one chart per PID sharing a time window.
- **Hooks and plugins:** a hooks API (`init`, `setData`, `draw`, `setCursor`, and so on) that everything else is built on.
- **Data format:** columnar arrays, `[timestamps_seconds, ys1, ys2, ...]`. Our `series` verb replies can map onto this directly, and `null` values draw gaps. That matters for sensor-unplug demos.

## What it doesn't include
- **Tooltips** beyond the legend. You write a small plugin (~30 lines).
- **Touch pan and pinch zoom.** Phone use needs a plugin or custom handlers.
- **Fetching, polling or state.** We still write all of that.
- **Non-time-series charts:** gauges, pies and heatmaps. The gauge would still be SVG or CSS.
- **Fault shading or event markers.** These are possible through the `draw` hook, but we write them.
- **Accessibility.** Canvas isn't readable by screen readers, so our table and verdict list carry that.

## What using it would mean for us
- **Vendoring:** the files are committed under something like `src/interface/vendor/uplot/`, with a pinned version, the LICENSE and a checksum in a README. There's no CDN, because the device is offline.
- **Embedding:** we serve it from the C binary like the rest of the page (`xxd -i` or `.incbin`). That adds about 50 KB to the binary, and we should serve it gzipped with `Content-Encoding: gzip`.
- **Tooling:** the vendored files need exclusions from markdownlint and cSpell (D-018), and probably a note in the repo that JS lives in `src/interface/`. That's a small gap to settle against CLAUDE.md §2.5, which scopes Python rather than JS.
- **Process:** third-party code in the tree is a ⚠️ UNREVIEWED decision, since a grader reading the tree should see it was a deliberate, recorded choice.
- **Defense:** it's the one piece of the front end we can't explain line by line. It's presentation only (nothing in analysis or storage), so I'd say that's acceptable, but the team should state it plainly.

## Versus inline SVG
| | Inline SVG (ours) | uPlot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Size | 0 KB, ~60 lines | ~50 KB vendored |
| Points per series | fine to ~2k; DOM slows after that | 100k+ |
| Zoom, hover, multi-axis | we write each | built in |
| Understood line by line | yes | no |
| Time we spend | ~half a day for sparklines | ~1–2 hours for first chart, plus plugins |

## My recommendation
- **Phase 1 (this PR):** SVG sparklines. With dummy data and a few dozen points per series, the SVG renders fine, and it keeps this PR free of third-party code.
- **Phase 2 (`phoneview`, M4):** switch to uPlot only if we want hours of history with zoom, since 48-hour soak data and "last drive" views are where SVG runs out. That would come with its own decision entry and board box.
- **Design for either:** in phase 1 I'd have the page hand `[ts[], ys[]]` arrays to a single `drawSeries(el, data)` function. Swapping SVG for uPlot then touches one function.

input.plan:
# Plan: `statusd`, the on-box status website (dummy data first)

## Context

D-013/D-028/D-043 already name this process: `statusd`, C, in `src/interface/`, the only
`AF_INET` process, serving the phone page over the box's own Wi-Fi. Board item `statusd`
(#177, "runs as a supervised child and is built by the Makefile") is the open box;
`phoneview` (M4) and `report` (M3) are the later content items. Today there is no server
code at all. The goal now: a working site showing faults/verdicts, process health, trends
and a CSV report, fed by **synthetic** values behind a seam, so the real OBD2/analysis data
plugs in later with no page changes.

Decisions already made with the user: server in **C** (matches D-043); **standalone
binary now**, supervisor spawning stays with `supfork` (#41); page scope = faults list,
process health, trends + CSV. A small "latest values" strip is included because trends are
meaningless without current readings (flag in review if unwanted).

## Design

**The seam (the whole point).** D-043 says the page is built from control-socket verbs
(`status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`; reply = `key=value` lines then `ok`). So
`statusd` talks to a *source* with one function: `source_query(verb, args, out_buf)`
returning exactly that D-043 text. Two implementations behind one header:
- `synth_source.c` (now): deterministic fake data, every record `src=synth`.
- `ctl_source.c` (later, not in this PR): connects to `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`.
Swapping = one line in `statusd_main.c`. No page or HTTP code changes.

**Routes** (HTTP/1.1, GET only, `Connection: close`, single-threaded `poll()`):

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | static page (HTML+CSS+JS embedded as C strings, no CDN: device is offline) |
| `/api/status` `/api/verdicts` `/api/series?pid=0C&from=..&to=..` `/api/faults` | the verb reply converted to JSON |
| `/report.csv` | CSV built from `series`+`verdicts`, `src` column on every row |
| anything else | 404; non-GET 405; oversized/malformed request 400 |

**Page.** Four panels, polled every 2 s with `fetch`: Latest values, Verdicts/faults
(active vs. past, fault area, cooperating sensors, residual), Process health
(supervisor/obdd/storaged/analyzed/statusd: up/down, uptime, restarts, RSS, ring depth),
Trends (inline-SVG sparklines per PID, drawn by ~60 lines of vanilla JS; no libraries).
A persistent banner shows **SYNTHETIC DATA** whenever any row has `src=synth` (CLAUDE.md
§2.7). Link to `/report.csv`. Read-only, no forms.

**Binding.** Default `127.0.0.1:8080` for development; `--bind ADDR` / `--port N` for the
AP address on the Pi (never defaults to `0.0.0.0`). Logs via `common/log.h`
(`log_init("statusd", ...)`, `log_set_src(SRC_SYNTH)`), every syscall error logged,
`goto`-cleanup, every allocation checked, no VLAs. SIGTERM exits 0 cleanly, heartbeat
via `log_heartbeat` so it is supervisable later (§2.6).

## Files

New (all under `src/interface/` unless noted):
- `statusd_main.c`: arg parsing, listen socket, poll loop, signals.
- `http.c` + `include/interface/http.h`: request-line parser and response writer (bounded buffers, header size cap, timeouts on slow clients).

# Plan: `statusd`, the on-box status website (dummy data first)

## Context

D-013/D-028/D-043 already name this process: `statusd`, C, in `src/interface/`, the only
`AF_INET` process, serving the phone page over the box's own Wi-Fi. Board item `statusd`
(#177, "runs as a supervised child and is built by the Makefile") is the open box;
`phoneview` (M4) and `report` (M3) are the later content items. Today there is no server
code at all. The goal now: a working site showing faults/verdicts, process health, trends
and a CSV report, fed by **synthetic** values behind a seam, so the real OBD2/analysis data
plugs in later with no page changes.

Decisions already made with the user: server in **C** (matches D-043); **standalone
binary now**, supervisor spawning stays with `supfork` (#41); page scope = faults list,
process health, trends + CSV. A small "latest values" strip is included because trends are
meaningless without current readings (flag in review if unwanted).

## Design

**The seam (the whole point).** D-043 says the page is built from control-socket verbs
(`status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`; reply = `key=value` lines then `ok`). So
`statusd` talks to a *source* with one function: `source_query(verb, args, out_buf)`
returning exactly that D-043 text. Two implementations behind one header:
- `synth_source.c` (now): deterministic fake data, every record `src=synth`.
- `ctl_source.c` (later, not in this PR): connects to `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`.
Swapping = one line in `statusd_main.c`. No page or HTTP code changes.

**Routes** (HTTP/1.1, GET only, `Connection: close`, single-threaded `poll()`):

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | static page (HTML+CSS+JS embedded as C strings, no CDN: device is offline) |
| `/api/status` `/api/verdicts` `/api/series?pid=0C&from=..&to=..` `/api/faults` | the verb reply converted to JSON |
| `/report.csv` | CSV built from `series`+`verdicts`, `src` column on every row |
| anything else | 404; non-GET 405; oversized/malformed request 400 |

**Page.** Four panels, polled every 2 s with `fetch`: Latest values, Verdicts/faults
(active vs. past, fault area, cooperating sensors, residual), Process health
(supervisor/obdd/storaged/analyzed/statusd: up/down, uptime, restarts, RSS, ring depth),
Trends (inline-SVG sparklines per PID, drawn by ~60 lines of vanilla JS; no libraries).
A persistent banner shows **SYNTHETIC DATA** whenever any row has `src=synth` (CLAUDE.md
§2.7). Link to `/report.csv`. Read-only, no forms.

**Binding.** Default `127.0.0.1:8080` for development; `--bind ADDR` / `--port N` for the
AP address on the Pi (never defaults to `0.0.0.0`). Logs via `common/log.h`
(`log_init("statusd", ...)`, `log_set_src(SRC_SYNTH)`), every syscall error logged,

content.text:
An "unreviewed" entry is how CLAUDE.md makes sure a human signs off on any decision Claude makes without them present.

**Why it exists**
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` is an audit log. Its job is to let you and Camden check after any session that nothing was decided on your behalf that you disagree with.
- Any decision I make without a human in the loop has to be written there as ⚠️ UNREVIEWED. It "binds nothing until a human signs it."
- I can never mark a decision reviewed or 🔒 LOCKED. Only you or Camden can, by editing the `Reviewed` field in a commit you author (CLAUDE.md §0, §7.7).
- You're present in this session, but the rule exists for what I choose between your instructions, and the choices below weren't explicitly yours.

**What an entry looks like.** I'd copy the shape of D-043, which is the closest sibling:
- A heading, e.g. `### B.13 — … ⚠️ UNREVIEWED`, then `D-045 · Drafted M3, <date> · By: Claude, in Lance's session · Reviewed: Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜`.
- **Decision**, **Why**, **Cost**, and **Alternative rejected** sections.
- One new row in the Review Queue table at the top of the file, saying who needs to review it and why. The queue is the first thing either of you reads after a session.

**What D-045 would record.** These are the things I decided that the repo didn't already say:
1. `statusd` is a server we write ourselves with no HTTP or web libraries. This rejects libmicrohttpd, Mongoose and CivetWeb, with the "no HTTP client" grep as the reason.
2. The page uses no JS or CSS libraries, and every chart goes through one `drawSeries` function so uPlot can replace it later.
3. The data source sits behind a seam that speaks D-043's reply format. A synthetic source feeds it now, with every row `src=synth`, and a `ctl.sock` client replaces it later.
4. `statusd` runs standalone until the supervisor's `supfork` work lands.

# Plan: `statusd`, the on-box status website (dummy data first)

## Context

D-013/D-028/D-043 already name this process: `statusd`, C, in `src/interface/`, the only
`AF_INET` process, serving the phone page over the box's own Wi-Fi. Board item `statusd`
(#177, "runs as a supervised child and is built by the Makefile") is the open box;
`phoneview` (M4) and `report` (M3) are the later content items. Today there is no server
code at all. The goal now: a working site showing faults/verdicts, process health, trends
and a CSV report, fed by **synthetic** values behind a seam, so the real OBD2/analysis data
plugs in later with no page changes.

Decisions already made with the user: server in **C** (matches D-043); **standalone
binary now**, supervisor spawning stays with `supfork` (#41); page scope = faults list,
process health, trends + CSV. A small "latest values" strip is included because trends are
meaningless without current readings (flag in review if unwanted).

## Design

**The seam (the whole point).** D-043 says the page is built from control-socket verbs
(`status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`; reply = `key=value` lines then `ok`). So
`statusd` talks to a *source* with one function: `source_query(verb, args, out_buf)`
returning exactly that D-043 text. Two implementations behind one header:
- `synth_source.c` (now): deterministic fake data, every record `src=synth`.
- `ctl_source.c` (later, not in this PR): connects to `/run/carwatch/ctl.sock`.
Swapping = one line in `statusd_main.c`. No page or HTTP code changes.

**Routes** (HTTP/1.1, GET only, `Connection: close`, single-threaded `poll()`):

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | static page (HTML+CSS+JS embedded as C strings, no CDN: device is offline) |
| `/api/status` `/api/verdicts` `/api/series?pid=0C&from=..&to=..` `/api/faults` | the verb reply converted to JSON |
| `/report.csv` | CSV built from `series`+`verdicts`, `src` column on every row |
| anything else | 404; non-GET 405; oversized/malformed request 400 |

**Page.** Four panels, polled every 2 s with `fetch`: Latest values, Verdicts/faults
(active vs. past, fault area, cooperating sensors, residual), Process health
(supervisor/obdd/storaged/analyzed/statusd: up/down, uptime, restarts, RSS, ring depth),
Trends (inline-SVG sparklines per PID, drawn by ~60 lines of vanilla JS; no libraries).
A persistent banner shows **SYNTHETIC DATA** whenever any row has `src=synth` (CLAUDE.md
§2.7). Link to `/report.csv`. Read-only, no forms.

**Binding.** Default `127.0.0.1:8080` for development; `--bind ADDR` / `--port N` for the
AP address on the Pi (never defaults to `0.0.0.0`). Logs via `common/log.h`
(`log_init("statusd", ...)`, `log_set_src(SRC_SYNTH)`), every syscall error logged,
`goto`-cleanup, every allocation checked, no VLAs. SIGTERM exits 0 cleanly, heartbeat
via `log_heartbeat` so it is supervisable later (§2.6).

## Files

New (all under `src/interface/` unless noted):
- `statusd_main.c`: arg parsing, listen socket, poll loop, signals.
- `http.c` + `include/interface/http.h`: request-line parser and response writer (bounded buffers, header size cap, timeouts on slow clients).
- `source.h`: the seam; `synth_source.c`: fake data (sine/random-walk RPM, speed, coolant, load, probe temp; 2 fake verdicts e.g. "cooling" and "intake/vacuum"; 5 fake process rows).
- `kv.c` + `include/interface/kv.h`: parse D-043 `key=value` reply lines; `json.c`: tiny JSON writer with escaping.
- `page.c`: embedded HTML/CSS/JS (or `src/interface/page/*.html` + a `make`-time generator, only if the embedded string gets unwieldy).
- Tests (same commit as each unit): `tests/test_http.c` (good/bad/oversized/partial requests), `tests/test_kv.c`, `tests/test_json.c` (escaping), `tests/test_statusd.c` (start on an ephemeral port, GET each route, check 200/404/405, `src=synth` present, CSV header).

Edits:
- `Makefile`: add `statusd` to `DAEMONS`, link rule `$(BIN)/statusd: $(BUILD)/src/interface/statusd_main.o $(COMMON_OBJ)`; change `COMMON_SRC` filter from `%/main.c` to `%main.c` so `statusd_main.c` stays out of the library; add `make run-status`.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md`: new ⚠️ UNREVIEWED entry (next free ID, "synthetic source seam; `statusd` standalone until `supfork`") **in the same commit as the code**, plus Review Queue row; `docs/DESIGN.md` §1 note; `docs/milestones.md`: add open boxes only (e.g. `ctlsource`: replace synth source with ctl.sock client; `statusspawn`: supervisor spawns statusd), never tick `statusd`. Then `python tools/board_sync.py`.
- `tests/boundary/`: no rule change expected (AF_INET only in `src/interface/` already passes); run it to confirm, and add a `good_` case only if the checker needs one.

Reuse: `common/log.h` (logging, `data_src_t`/`SRC_SYNTH`, `log_heartbeat`); `Makefile` test globbing picks up new `tests/test_*.c` automatically; existing `tools/obdsim.py` is *not* used (that emulates the adapter, a different layer).

## Commit sequence (CLAUDE.md §7; branch `lance/m3/statusd`, draft PR at first commit)

Session is **Lance's**. Branch from fresh `main` before any edit. Stage explicit paths only.
Tests lead: in each commit the test is written first and seen failing. Each commit builds
and passes `make`, `make test`, `make asan` on its own.

1. `M3 interface: parse HTTP requests and write responses`
   `http.c`, `include/interface/http.h`, `tests/test_http.c`. Pure functions, no sockets:
   parse a request line (GET only) and headers out of a byte buffer, reporting
   incomplete / bad / too large; format a response with status, `Content-Type`,
   `Content-Length`. Tests: good GET, partial read, bad method (405), garbage (400),
   header over the size cap, embedded NULs, path with `..`.
2. `M3 interface: parse control-socket reply lines`
   `kv.c`, `include/interface/kv.h`, `tests/test_kv.c`. Reads the D-043 reply format
   (`key=value` lines, then `ok` or `err <code> <reason>`) into a bounded struct. Tests:
   normal reply, `err`, missing terminator, over-long line, empty value.
3. `M3 interface: write JSON with escaping`
   `json.c`, `include/interface/json.h`, `tests/test_json.c`. Tiny writer into a bounded
   buffer: objects, arrays, strings with quote/backslash/control-char escaping, and a
   truncation error rather than overflow. Separate from 2 because it is a different
   yes/no: the parser reads, this writes.
4. `M3 interface: synthetic data source behind the control-socket seam`
   `source.h`, `synth_source.c`, `tests/test_synth_source.c`. `source_query(verb, args,
   out)` returns D-043-format text for `status`, `verdicts`, `series`, `faults`. Values
   are deterministic from a time argument (so tests are exact) and every row carries
   `src=synth`. Test asserts that no reply line lacks `src=synth` and that replies parse
   with commit 2's parser.
5. `M3 interface: serve the status API from statusd`
   `statusd_main.c`, Makefile (`statusd` in `DAEMONS`, `%main.c` filter, `make
   run-status`), `tests/test_statusd.c`, and draft decision D-045 (own server, no
   libraries, synth seam, standalone until `supfork`; uPlot deferred) with its
   Review Queue row, in this same commit (CLAUDE.md §7.7). `poll()` loop, `--bind` /
   `--port`, per-connection deadline, SIGTERM exits 0, `log_heartbeat`. Routes
   `/api/status|verdicts|series|faults` via commits 1-4; `/` is a one-line placeholder.
   Likely over 400 lines; `WHY` will say it is the first commit that is a runnable
   process and the decision cannot precede it.
6. `M3 interface: add the CSV report route`
   `/report.csv` built from `series` + `verdicts`, `src` column on every row, header row,
   CSV field quoting. Tests extend `test_statusd.c`. Separate because it is its own
   output format with its own quoting rules (D-028).
7. `M3 interface: add the status page`
   `page.c`: embedded HTML/CSS/JS, vanilla. Panels: latest values, verdicts/faults,
   process health, trends. All charts go through one `drawSeries(el, ts, ys)` function
   (SVG polyline) so uPlot can replace it later. Persistent SYNTHETIC DATA banner driven
   by the `src` field. Test: `/` returns the page with the banner element and the
   script; manual check in a phone-width browser.
8. `M3 docs: board boxes for the real source and supervisor spawn`
   `docs/milestones.md` open boxes (`ctlsource`: replace the synth source with a
   ctl.sock client; `statusspawn`: supervisor starts statusd; `uplot`: revisit charting
   at phoneview), a DESIGN.md §1 note, then `python3 tools/board_sync.py`. Does not tick
   `statusd`; a human does that.

PR title follows commit 5's lead claim, opened as a draft at commit 1.

## Verification

- `make`, `make test` (includes `boundary`, `boardcheck`, `toolcheck`), `make asan`: all green, output pasted in the PR. Note `python` is not on PATH here (only `python3`), so run `python3 tools/board_sync.py`.
- Manual: `make run-status`, open `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`; confirm the SYNTHETIC banner, panels update every 2 s, `curl -i` each route, `curl /report.csv | head` shows `src=synth` on every row, bad inputs (`printf 'GARBAGE\r\n\r\n' | nc 127.0.0.1 8080`, a 100 KB header, a slow client) get 400/closed without crashing.
- `kill -TERM` exits 0; `kill -9` leaves no stray fds (`ls /proc/<pid>/fd` before/after).
- Run with the network unplugged on loopback to confirm no outbound calls (`ss -tp` shows only the listener).

## Least sure about / for review

- Single-threaded `poll()` is enough for one phone; a slow client is handled by a per-connection deadline, which needs a test.
- Embedded page strings are reviewable but awkward; split to files if it passes ~300 lines.
- The "latest values" strip was not in the chosen scope; cheap to drop.
- The new decision is ⚠️ UNREVIEWED until Camden or Lance signs it.

I created the branch `lance/m3/statusd` from up-to-date `main`, and the tree is clean. I haven't written any code yet. Here is `http.c` method by method. It does no I/O, only bytes in and bytes out, so every function is testable without a socket.

**`include/interface/http.h`**

| Item | Signature | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| limits | `HTTP_MAX_REQUEST 4096`, `HTTP_PATH_MAX 128`, `HTTP_QUERY_MAX 256` | Hard caps. All buffers are fixed-size, so no allocation and nothing to leak. |
| `http_parse_t` | enum: `HTTP_OK`, `HTTP_INCOMPLETE`, `HTTP_BAD`, `HTTP_BAD_METHOD`, `HTTP_TOO_LARGE` | Every parse outcome. The caller never inspects bytes itself. |
| `http_request_t` | `{ char path[HTTP_PATH_MAX]; char query[HTTP_QUERY_MAX]; }` | The result. The method is always GET, and headers are validated but not kept. |
| `http_parse_request` | `(const char *buf, size_t len, http_request_t *out) → http_parse_t` | See below. |
| `http_status_for` | `(http_parse_t) → int` | `BAD`→400, `BAD_METHOD`→405, `TOO_LARGE`→431. Keeps the mapping in one place. |
| `http_query_get` | `(const char *query, const char *key, char *out, size_t n) → int` | Finds `key=value` in `a=1&b=2`, percent-decodes it, and returns 0 or -1. Needed for `series?pid=0C&from=-2h`, where ISO 8601 times contain `:` and `+`. |
| `http_write_head` | `(char *out, size_t cap, int status, const char *ctype, size_t body_len) → ssize_t` | Writes the status line and headers only, returning the length or -1 if `cap` is too small. The caller sends the body separately, so the embedded page is never copied. |

**`http_parse_request` behavior**
1. It looks for the `\r\n\r\n` that ends the headers.
   - If it isn't there and `len >= HTTP_MAX_REQUEST`, return `TOO_LARGE`.
   - If it isn't there and `len` is smaller, return `INCOMPLETE`. The caller reads more and calls again, which handles partial reads.
2. It parses the request line as `GET SP target SP HTTP/1.0|1.1`.
   - Any other method returns `BAD_METHOD` (405). Anything malformed returns `BAD`.
3. It rejects the target if any of these hold:
   - It has a NUL or a control character.
   - It doesn't start with `/`.
   - It contains a `..` path segment.
   - It is over a cap.
4. It splits the target at `?` into `path` and `query`, without decoding yet. Decoding happens in `http_query_get`, so a `%2e%2e` can't sneak a `..` past the path check.
5. It checks the header lines for NULs and control characters only. We don't read any header, so a bad one is a 400.

**`http_write_head` output**: `HTTP/1.1 <status> <text>`, then `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Connection: close`, `Cache-Control: no-store` (stale vitals on a phone would be misleading), and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.  What do you mean by HEAD, is that the device info?

No, `HEAD` isn't device info. It's one of the standard HTTP request methods, like `GET` or `POST`.

**What it is**
- The method is the first word of a request line, such as `GET /api/status HTTP/1.1`.
- `GET` means "send me this resource."
- `HEAD` means "send me the same response you'd send for a `GET`, but only the headers, with no body."
- So `HEAD /api/status` would return `200 OK`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and the other headers, then stop.

**Who uses it**
- Link checkers and monitoring scripts, to ask "is this alive, and how big is it?" without downloading the body.
- Some proxies and caches.
- A browser loading our page never sends it, and neither does our JavaScript's `fetch()` unless we ask it to.
- You can send one by hand with `curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8080/`.

**What allowing it would cost**
- The parser would accept `HEAD` and the server would send the headers without the body.
- Every route would need a "was this HEAD?" flag so the body is skipped, and the `Content-Length` still has to match what a `GET` would send. That's one more case to test, on a path that has no user.

**Why I lean toward refusing it**
- Nothing in our plan sends it.
- Refusing it keeps the rule easy to state: "GET only, anything else is 405." That's easy to defend and easy to show in a live modification.
- If a monitoring tool ever needs it, adding it later is a small change.

The 405 reply for `HEAD` is also legitimate under the HTTP spec, as long as we send an `Allow: GET` header. I'll add that header to the 405 response, because the spec says a 405 should carry it. That's a small addition to `http_write_head`.

Both are fair questions. Nothing has been written to disk yet.

**Why `HTTP_OK` returns 0 and not 200**
- `http_status_for` answers "what status do I send *because the parse was refused*?" A successful parse doesn't decide the response status.
- Once a request parses, the route decides: `/api/status` gets 200, an unknown path gets 404, and a handler failure gets 500. The parser doesn't know any of that, so returning 200 would be a wrong promise.
- `INCOMPLETE` isn't a response at all, because we're still waiting for bytes.
- Using 0 as "no refusal" is a sentinel, and it's the weakest part of that function. A caller who forgets to check the parse result and passes 0 to `http_write_head` gets -1 back, since 0 isn't a known status. It fails loudly, but it's still a design smell.

**Why there are two mapping functions**
They answer different questions:
- `http_status_for` goes from parse outcome to number: `HTTP_BAD_METHOD` → 405.
- `status_text` goes from number to reason phrase: 405 → `"Method Not Allowed"`. This is the text in `HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed`.
- It's `static` because only `http_write_head` uses it. It returns a pointer to a string literal, which lives in read-only memory, so there's no allocation and nothing to free. It returns NULL for a code we don't know, and that is how `http_write_head` refuses unsupported statuses.
- The phrase is cosmetic, because clients key off the number. But the line is conventionally written with it, and curl output reads better.

**What I'd simplify**
- Drop `http_status_for` and `HTTP_OK`/`HTTP_INCOMPLETE` sentinel handling. The caller would `switch` on the parse result in `statusd_main.c`: `INCOMPLETE` means keep reading, `OK` means route it, and every other value maps to its status. That puts the mapping next to the only code that uses it.
- Alternatively, keep it in `http.c` but make the enum values the codes (`HTTP_BAD = 400`, and so on). Then no mapping function exists at all, and `OK` and `INCOMPLETE` become negative or zero values. It's compact but clever, and a reviewer has to know the trick.
- `status_text` stays as a small `switch`. A table of `{code, text}` is the other option, but with six entries the `switch` reads fine.

I'd go with the first option: remove `http_status_for` and the test for it, and let the caller switch.

M3 interface: parse HTTP requests and write response heads

WHAT:   http.c parses a GET request out of a byte buffer (complete, incomplete or refused),

        before any socket exists. cspell gains "nosniff", a header value it writes.

        "%2e%2e" cannot pass, and every refusal path in the test. Least sure: HTTP/1.0 and
        1.1 only, and the 4096-byte cap are my choices, not from a decision yet.
VERIFY: make, make test, make asan all exit 0; test_http PASS under ASan and UBSan.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

  release, the restarted process sees that batch again. So every batch also records, as
  an event, the `seq` of the newest ring slot it holds, and each run records which ring
  instance it drains (its generation, set at creation). After a restart, `storaged` skips
  slots at or below the last committed ring `seq`, but only for the same ring instance:
  a ring made fresh at the next boot is never skipped. A batch is never written twice.

**Why.** With `ring_pop`, a slot left the ring the moment `storaged` read it, up to a
second before it was durable (D-035), so killing `storaged` (the soak's injected fault,
mechanism E's test) silently lost those samples, the loss B.3 exists to prevent. A
shared-memory ring that any child re-initializes on restart would reset the other side's
indices; a header check stops a ring left over from an older build being read with a new
layout.

**Cost.** A ring holds at most 4096 slots, about 200 s at 20 samples a second, so a
`storaged` that is down longer makes the producer refuse (counted, B.3). Two small events
per batch (the ring generation once per run, the newest ring `seq` per batch). A first
draft skipped by `mono_ns` instead; the restart test lost a sample to two readings with
the same timestamp, which ring `seq` cannot have.

81	## A. Hardware and interfaces
82	
83	### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 over a Bluetooth Classic adapter; USB is the fallback ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
84	
85	`D-019` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
86	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
87	· **Supersedes:** D-015 (§G.4)
88	
89	*Pi power revised 2026-10-21 by D-024 (§A.6), before any review: the Pi is in a box fed
90	by the owner's USB-C charger, not wired to the car's USB. The adapter's key-off draw is
91	now board item `dongledrain`.*
92	
93	**Decision.** An **OBDLink LX** (STN chip, **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile**; not
94	BLE) plugs into the OBD2 port. The Pi, in the box (D-024), talks to it with
95	its built-in Bluetooth radio over RFCOMM. Provisioning pairs and trusts the adapter once,
96	binds it with `rfcomm bind` to `/dev/rfcomm0`, and a udev rule links that to **`/dev/obd`**,
97	so every consumer still opens `/dev/obd` and sends Mode 01 requests (D-012). No MCP2515, no
98	SPI, no CAN wiring, and no data cable in the cabin.
99	
100	**Raw CAN is still a stretch goal**: an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D
101	and E are implemented *and measured* (unchanged from D-015).
102	
103	**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23: the goal is the simplest data path that works. The box
104	becomes one power cable; the adapter stays in the port. The protocol, the parsing and every
105	downstream design are the same as D-015, because an STN adapter speaks the same ELM327
106	command set over Bluetooth as over USB.
107	
108	*Note 2026-10-27: D-038 rewrote `make boundary`. `AF_BLUETOOTH` is now banned everywhere,
109	and Unix sockets are allowed through `src/ipc/uds.c`, so the reasoning below still holds.*
110	
111	**Why a tty and not our own Bluetooth socket.** Opening an RFCOMM socket from `obdd` would
112	put `socket()` in `src/obd/`, which `make boundary` forbids outside `src/interface/`
113	(CLAUDE.md §2.1). Letting the kernel's RFCOMM layer present a tty keeps the boundary check
114	meaningful and keeps `obdd` a plain serial reader.
115	
116	**What D-001 (§G.1) said against this, and why it no longer applies.** G.1 rejected a
117	Bluetooth ELM327 because it gives up interrupts and bus-level timing, taking mechanisms A,
118	B, C and F with it. D-015 already accepted exactly that loss for the USB adapter, and D-017
119	records what survives (D and E). Bluetooth costs no further mechanism.
120	
121	**Costs and risks.**
122	
123	- **Provisioning.** Pairing, trust and a persistent bind must survive reboots and every
124	  key-off (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`, board item `bench`).
125	- **A new failure mode.** The link can drop while the engine runs (adapter out of range,
126	  adapter asleep, radio interference). `obdd` sees a hangup on the tty and must reconnect
127	  with backoff, not crash-loop (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4, `supbackoff`).
128	- **One radio, two jobs.** The Pi 4's single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip also runs the phone
129	  access point (D-013). Coexistence is expected to work but is unmeasured: board item
130	  `btcoex`. Putting the access point on 5 GHz is the first mitigation to try.
131	- **Key-off draw.** The adapter still draws from OBD2 pin 16, live with the key off, and a
132	  Bluetooth adapter keeps a radio up. Its sleep behavior and key-off current are measured
133	  before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).
134	
135	**Fallback.** The USB adapter of D-015 (§G.4) needs only a different udev rule to appear as
136	`/dev/obd`. If Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car, switching back is a provisioning
137	change, not a code change.
138	
139	### A.2 — Testbeds: Camden's 2008 Forester and Lance's 2015 CR-V ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
140	
141	`D-022` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
142	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
143	· **Supersedes:** D-016 (§G.6) · **Amends:** the claim wording of D-021 (§E.1)
144	
145	**Decision.** Two cars are available as testbeds: Camden's **2008 Subaru Forester**
146	(non-turbo) and Lance's **2015 Honda CR-V EX-L** (D-007). Neither car is required of
147	anyone, and either partner tests wherever suits them. Every capture records which car it
148	came from.
149	
150	**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P1): a car on Camden's
151	own schedule lets live capture start without waiting on anyone, and no document should
152	restrict where either partner tests. The device learns whichever car it is installed in,
153	so a second car costs no code.
154	
155	**The claim, reworded.** D-021's *"this CR-V"* becomes *"the car it is installed in"*
156	(§E.1). Results are reported per car and labeled with the car.
157	
158	**Cost.**
159	
160	- Each car needs its own PID survey (`pidforester`, `pidhonda`). The two sensor lists may
161	  differ, and the Forester's OBD protocol is not verified: a 2008 US car is expected to
162	  speak CAN (ISO 15765-4), but MAP, for one, may be absent.
163	- Baselines are per car. Two cars split the calendar time of normal driving unless one of
164	  them carries most of it.
165	
166	**Alternative rejected.** Keeping D-016 (the CR-V only): every live capture would wait on
167	one car's schedule.
168

170	
171	`D-007` · **Owner:** Lance · **Tracked as:** GitHub issue `honda` (label `question`)

179	
180	**What the answer changes.**
181	
182	- **No Honda Sensing on the EX-L** (it was Touring-only in 2015), so there is no
183	  lane-keep camera connector to tap. The OBD2 port is the tap point (**D-024**).

185	  practice). Under D-021 that only removes one sensor from the list; nothing depends on it.
186	- **The Honda has Maintenance Minder**, an oil-life estimate from how the engine has been

196	### A.4 — Capture the schematic in KiCad; do not fabricate a PCB 🔒
197	
198	`D-009` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
199	
200	*Note 2026-10-27, not a reopening: the MCP2515 named below is now a stretch goal only
201	(D-019), and owners are per D-026. `make hwdocs` emits the schematic SVG, `bom.csv` and a
202	netlist; `BOM.md` and `wiring.md` are still written by hand and checked against them.*
203	
204	**Decision.** We draw the full schematic in KiCad (`electricalDrawing/`, KiCad 10, owned
205	by Lance) and treat it as the source of truth for wiring and the BOM. We do **not**
206	fabricate a custom PCB unless we take The Reach (handout §14). The empty `.kicad_pcb`
207	stays in the repo on purpose.
208	
209	**Why.** A custom board earns zero points — the rubric grades mechanisms, measurements and
210	the soak — and fab turnaround lands on top of critical path B, already the likeliest cause
211	of an M2 slip. A breadboard plus an off-the-shelf MCP2515 module clears every guardrail, and
212	the handout is explicit that a food container is an acceptable enclosure.
213	
214	**Why the schematic is still worth the hours.** Three graded artifacts depend on it:
215	`docs/DESIGN.md` needs a defensible wiring story; `docs/hardware/wiring.md` needs pin assignments
216	that cannot drift from the build; and the three-isolated-workers test needs a parts-only
217	buyer who can order from the BOM without seeing the design. A hand-maintained pin table will
218	disagree with reality by Week 9. A generated one cannot.
219	
220	**Consequences.** `make hwcheck` (ERC) and `make hwdocs` (SVG, BOM, netlist) enter the
221	build. `docs/hardware/wiring.md` and `BOM.md` become **derived** artifacts. `CLAUDE.md`
222	§7.12 requires a rendered schematic in any PR touching hardware.
223	
224	### A.5 — ERC is a build failure, and the schematic SVG is committed 🔒
225	
226	`D-010` · Decided M0 · **By:** Camden + Claude · **Reviewed:** Camden ✅ / Lance ⬜
227	
228	*Note 2026-10-27, not a reopening: nothing has been drawn yet, so `docs/figures/` and its
229	SVG do not exist; the first PR that draws a block commits them (`hwgate`).*
230	
231	**Decision.** `kicad-cli sch erc --exit-code-violations` runs as `make hwcheck`; violations
232	fail the build. `make hwdocs` renders the schematic to `docs/figures/electricalDrawing.svg`,
233	and that SVG is **committed**.
234	
235	**Why the ERC gate.** It makes electrical correctness the same kind of object as
236	`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`: a machine-checked precondition rather than a thing someone
237	remembers to look at. Unconnected pins and power-output conflicts are exactly the class of
238	error that survives a human read and kills a board.
239	
240	**Why commit a generated file.** Normally we would not. But a reviewer cannot read a diff
241	of S-expression coordinates, and §7.6 says a PR nobody understands does not merge — so
242	without a rendered picture, hardware would fall outside the review process entirely. The
243	SVG is the diff a human can actually read. It is regenerated, never hand-edited.
244	
245	**Open sub-item (Lance, M2):** `sym-lib-table` referenced `CS370_Project_Library.kicad_sym`,
246	which did not exist — KiCad errors on project open. An empty library is committed to resolve
247	it; populate it as parts are drawn.
248	
249	### A.6 — One box, one USB-C input, and a seconds-scale supercapacitor ⚠️ UNREVIEWED
250	
251	`D-024` · Decided M2, 2026-10-21 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
252	· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
253	· **Supersedes:** D-011 (§G.9) · **Revises:** D-019's "the Pi, powered from the car's USB"
254	
255	**Decision.** The product is one small box, plus the Bluetooth OBD2 dongle (D-019) in the
256	car's OBD2 port.
257	
258	- **One port.** A single USB-C receptacle is the box's only power input. The owner plugs
259	  it into whatever USB-C charger and cable they already have in the car. The box is a
260	  plain sink (5.1 kΩ on both CC pins), so no source offers it more than 5 V.
261	- **One light, no buttons, no other ports** (light: D-027). Nothing on the car is cut,
262	  spliced, pierced or clamped.
263	- **Off at rest.** The box runs only while its source is live. At key-off the source
264	  disappears; the box sees it on a source-present GPIO, waits out a short grace period,
265	  commits and checkpoints its storage, and halts. The power stage then cuts the Pi's
266	  supply, and the box stays dark until the next start, when it boots by itself.
267	- **A small supercapacitor bank** covers brief shortfalls, rides through the dip at
268	  engine start where it can, and powers the clean shutdown. A seconds-scale bank cannot
269	  make up for a source that is too weak for a whole drive; see the limits below. It is
270	  short-lived by design: the goal is seconds to tens of seconds of runtime, about one
271	  minute is the ceiling, and it is never an always-on supply.
272	- **Clean shutdown is the normal path; crash consistency is the guarantee.** If the bank
273	  is empty, the cable is pulled or the Pi resets at crank, storage recovers at the next
274	  boot (mechanism D).
275	
276	**The power block's requirements.** Parts come only from datasheets a human has checked
277	(`CLAUDE.md` §8.4), and nothing is ordered until the design is signed.
278	
279	1. Sink only, 5 V only; transient and reverse-polarity protection; a fuse.
280	2. An input current limit below what the source advertises, and an inrush limiter,
281	   because an empty bank looks like a short circuit. A plain sink does not know the
282	   source's rating, so the box reads the source's CC advertisement (USB default, 1.5 A or
283	   3 A). The Pi has no analog inputs, so that takes a detector part (comparators or a
284	   USB-C controller IC) that reports the level on GPIOs.
285	3. Power path: the source feeds the Pi first; the bank covers only the shortfall or the
286	   gap.
287	4. A source-present signal on a GPIO, divided down to 3.3 V.
288	5. A halt-done signal: once the Pi has halted, the power stage removes the Pi's supply
289	   **even if the source has come back**, holds it off briefly, then re-enables. Otherwise
290	   a source that returns mid-shutdown leaves a halted Pi and a dark box in a running car.
291	6. Auto power-on when the source returns, with no button.
292	7. A 5 V, 3 A converter to the Pi that can step up, because the bank's voltage falls as it
293	   discharges.
294	
295	**Estimates, not measurements.** Each is replaced by a measured value before it appears
296	in `docs/DESIGN.md` as anything but an estimate (`powerspec`, `capbench`).
297	
298	| Quantity | Estimate |
299	| --- | --- |
300	| Pi 4 draw during boot and shutdown | 3 to 5 W |
301	| Grace period before shutdown starts (longer than a crank dip) | about 3 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 ≈ 15 J |
302	| Clean-shutdown energy | 10–15 s × 4 W ÷ 0.85 converter efficiency ≈ 50–70 J |
303	| Crank-bridge energy | 1–3 s × 5 W ≈ 5–15 J |
304	| Two 2.7 V cells in series, 10 F total, charged to about 5 V | ½·C·V² ≈ 125 J stored; about 105 J usable above a 2 V converter floor, about 20 s at 4 W |
305	| Charge time from empty at a 1 A budget | 10 F × 5 V ÷ 1 A ≈ 50 s; slower on a 1.5 A source that is also running the Pi |
306	
307	The margin is thin: grace plus shutdown come to about 65–85 J against about 105 J usable,
308	before the radios' draw is counted. `powerspec` replaces every row with a measurement and
309	states the margin.
310	
311	**Limits, stated plainly.**
312	
313	- **Cold start.** The bank is empty at the first key-on of a session, so it cannot bridge
314	  that crank dip, and the Pi may reset while cranking. That is survivable only because
315	  storage is crash-consistent. Crank bridging is best-effort; the key-off shutdown is the
316	  reliable path.
317	- **Always-live sources are not supported.** On a charger that stays live with the key
318	  off, the box stays on, and the Pi plus the dongle can drain the car's battery over a few
319	  days. This is an installation requirement, not a mode we engineer around, but whether
320	  the box should halt itself after a long stretch with the engine silent is open
321	  (`shutfsm`).
322	- **Weak sources.** A charger that advertises only default USB current (500 or 900 mA)
323	  cannot run a Pi 4 with both radios, and the bank cannot make up the difference for a
324	  whole drive. What the box does then (refuse to start and show red, or run degraded) is
325	  open (`powerspec`).
326	- **Boot time.** A stock Pi 4 boots in roughly half a minute (estimate, `bootbudget`), so
327	  the start of each drive's warm-up goes unrecorded.
328	- **Demo day.** The box is off unless powered, and the handout's live demonstration runs
329	  on live sensors (§5, §11), so the demo needs a running testbed car on site, or an
330	  arrangement with the professor (`democar`).
331	- **The dongle still draws from OBD2 pin 16 with the key off** (D-019). Its key-off
332	  current is measured before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).
333	
334	**Why one box.** Camden's design, 2026-10-21 (`docs/REVISION_PLAN.md` §1.1, P7–P10,
335	P13): "no need to reinvent the charger." The owner already has a USB-C charger, so the
336	team designs the box and buys only the dongle and a cable. One port and one light is a
337	product an ordinary owner can install.
338	
339	**Why a supercapacitor.** Camden's choice, 2026-10-21 (R1). A lithium cell must not
340	charge above about 45 °C or below 0 °C, and a car cabin leaves that window at both ends;
341	many cheap Pi UPS boards have no temperature cutoff. A supercapacitor has no
342	thermal-runaway failure, tolerates a wider temperature range (confirm against the part's
343	datasheet), and fits a seconds-scale job. Its costs are low voltage per cell (two in
344	series, with balancing), very low internal resistance (so a fuse), and fast
345	self-discharge, which does not matter for a box that is off at rest.
346	
347	**Alternatives rejected.** The car's USB wired straight to the Pi (D-011): no warning
348	before power loss, so every key-off cut a write. A small lithium cell: the charge
349	temperature window above. A wake button: dropped (P10).
350	
351	**Cost.** A power block to design, draw, buy and bench-test, on the hardware critical
352	path (`powerspec`, `schpower`, `capbench`), and more to measure before any claim
353	(`keyoff`, `cranklog`, `expshut`).
